Case: Patient D is a 77-year-old Black man with history of lung cancer who presents with 3 months of diffuse back pain and progressive, unintentional weight loss. Patient D describes the pain as constant and exacerbated by bending and twisting movements of his spine. In addition to increasing pain, he endorses progressive diffuse weakness, and he now to requires a front-wheel-walker to ambulate. Upon examining Patient D, you find that he is cachetic and diffusely deconditioned. You palpate the full length of his spine and note that he is diffusely tender.
